name: Jeush
overview: Jeush was a male Edomite, notable as a son of Esau and a chief of Edom. His identity is grounded in his tribal affiliation with the Edomites and his leadership role among them. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeush means '[perhaps] may G-d aid,' reflecting a possible invocation of divine assistance. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaningful Hebrew connotation.
familyAndRelationships: Jeush is recorded as a son of Esau and Judith, establishing his place within the Edomite lineage. Scripture does not provide further family relationships beyond these parental connections.
scriptureSignificance: Jeush holds significance as a direct descendant of Esau, the progenitor of the Edomites, and as a chief within the Edomite nation. His mention underscores the continuation of Esau's lineage and the establishment of leadership among the Edomites. This highlights the biblical theme of God's providential unfolding of nations through family lines.
